GGRS26CombattingGerrymanderingRCV.Ballot.reason: An election update is the source STV surplus-transfer operation on actual ballots supporting the elected candidate; it is an admissible rule law, not a supplied tally or outcome.
For each legal quota election, the transfer policy supplies an admissible post-election ballot-weight update; this records the source procedure rather than assuming a terminal outcome.
A legal election update preserves nonnegative remaining ballot weight on the finite electorate, as required by the physical surplus-transfer interpretation.
A legal quota election removes exactly one quota from the elected candidate's supporting ballot mass, matching the source rule that transfers only the surplus.

On an election, a ballot supporting the winner retains or transfers part of its own remaining mass but never gains weight; this is physical ballot semantics, not aggregate conservation asserted from the result.
An election update leaves a ballot that does not support the elected candidate unchanged, so the source transfer acts only through the winner's support.
An elimination update reroutes each affected ballot to its next active preference while keeping the source ranked-ballot state explicit.
For each legal elimination, the policy supplies an admissible rerouting update; this is part of the source STV procedure and does not presuppose an outcome.
Elimination changes the active preference route but preserves each ballot's remaining weight, as in the source transfer description.
A quota-election branch selects a currently active candidate, matching the source count's candidate-status rule.
A quota-election branch removes the elected candidate from the active roster; it does not encode which party ultimately wins seats.
A quota-election branch records the elected candidate in the elected roster, matching the source round update.
A quota-election transition is allowed only before the source stopping condition holds.
A quota-election branch requires the selected active candidate to meet the Droop quota stated in the source procedure.
A quota-election branch applies while an additional seat remains to be filled, matching the source round semantics.
A quota-election branch uses an update satisfying the separately audited physical surplus-transfer law.
An elimination branch selects a currently active candidate, as required by the source count.
An elimination branch removes exactly the eliminated candidate from the active roster.
An elimination branch leaves the elected roster unchanged, so elimination does not smuggle a winner declaration.
An elimination branch selects a minimum current active tally, as the source STV procedure specifies.
An elimination branch is available only when no active candidate meets quota, preserving the source quota-first order.
An elimination transition is allowed only before the source stopping condition holds.
An elimination branch uses an update satisfying the separately audited ballot rerouting law.

semantic-model::paper_proposition1_all_b.reason: The direct endpoint is alpha-checked against its transparent specification and compared with the pinned source model. The review uses expanded propositions, exact manifest atoms, source anchors, and checked bridges rather than theorem, binder, record, or field names. The positive-share restriction is the separately approved convention; the two-party active-candidate universe is a source-supported model interpretation, not a silently literal display premise.

carrier_and_domain.lean_bridge: PaperInterface.lean:996-1004 constructs the finite-electorate unit-weight state, and :1067-1108 proves a terminal execution from exactly that state and policy.
carrier_and_domain.lean_evidence: The finite ballot-weight state, quota-first election/minimum-tally elimination relation, and transfer laws are exposed in BallotRoutedSTV.lean:28-202. The source-facing initial state, terminal-execution bridge, transparent specification, and direct endpoint are in PaperInterface.lean:996-1249.
carrier_and_domain.semantic_comparison: The source's district electorate and candidate rosters are finite. Lean represents them by finite sets and constructs unit ballot weight only on the declared electorate; values outside it are not read. The source-supported two-party universe requires the active roster to be covered by the two party rosters, so no third active party is silently admitted.
